record.paper_title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let G be a polycyclic group and let phi be an endomorphism of G. Given elements w and t in G with the promise that at least one element a in G satisfies t = a^-1 w phi(a), determine the computational complexity of finding such an element a. Equivalently, determine the complexity of the twisted conjugacy search problem in polycyclic groups.

evidence.quote: The twisted conjugacy search problems is to find, given a group G and an endomorphism φ, an element a ∈ G such that t = a−1 wφ(a), provided that at least one such a exists.
(2) What is the complexity of the twisted search conjugacy problem in poly- cyclic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called polycyclic if it admits a subnormal series $G = G_0 \trianglerighteq G_1 \trianglerighteq \cdots \trianglerighteq G_n = \{1\}$ in which every quotient $G_i/G_{i+1}$ is cyclic. Fix a polycyclic group $G$ given by a finite polycyclic presentation, and let $\varphi : G \to G$ be an endomorphism specified by the images of the generators.

The twisted conjugacy search problem is the following computational task: given elements $w, t \in G$ together with the promise that there exists at least one element $a \in G$ with
$$ t = a^{-1}\, w\, \varphi(a), $$
produce such an element $a$.

Determine the computational complexity of the twisted conjugacy search problem in the class of polycyclic groups. In particular, exhibit an algorithm together with rigorous complexity bounds (as a function of the input size, measured for instance by the lengths of $w$, $t$, and the description of $\varphi$), or prove hardness lower bounds for this search problem.
artifact.status_search_result: Decidability of the twisted conjugacy problem in polycyclic(-by-finite) groups has been established and practical algorithms have been implemented (e.g., the GAP TwistedConjugacy package by Tertooy, 2020), but no precise complexity bounds for the twisted conjugacy search problem in general polycyclic groups appear in the literature. Related results show the ordinary conjugacy search problem can be NP-hard in certain polycyclic families, suggesting the twisted version is at least as hard, but a sharp complexity characterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: Algorithms for twisted conjugacy classes of polycyclic-by-finite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Practical algorithms to determine whether two elements are twisted conjugate, under conditions on Reidemeister coincidence number.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithms exist but without sharp complexity analysis for the general search problem.

status_evidence.title: A family of polycyclic groups over which the uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete
status_evidence.snippet: Polycyclic groups where conjugacy search is at least as hard as subset sum.
status_evidence.claim: Conjugacy search in polycyclic groups can be NP-hard, hinting at hardness for the twisted variant.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of Conjugacy Search in some Polycyclic and Matrix Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies various versions of the conjugacy search problem in polycyclic groups.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity of search variants in polycyclic groups remains an active area without a definitive answer.
